free_tier.stated: Unlimited projects and domains, with publishing under rate limits that apply to every plan

per_object_cap.stated: Projects are limited to 10,100 files and 450 MB; a larger project is refused before anything is published.
per_object_cap.notes: Projects are limited to 10,100 files and 450 MB; a larger project is refused before anything is published.

retention.notes: Every publish creates a new revision (Surge keeps the last 100).

egress.terms: Every project—Free or Pro—serves from all of them.

tooling: Official `surge` CLI (npm, ~free) and a documented raw REST deploy API: PUT /:domain with Basic auth, Content-Type: application/gzip, a gzipped tarball body plus file-count and project-size headers. That is directly scriptable, no CLI needed.
chaining: There's no cap on how many projects or domains you publish, but how often you publish is rate limited.

limits.value: no per-file cap documented but it inherits the project cap

limits_note: 450 MB and 10,100 files per project (hard: 'Aborted - Unable to publish. Application too large'); no bandwidth figure published; no per-file cap documented but it inherits the project cap. Re-publishing replaces the whole project (full-sync deploy), so appending one file re-uploads the directory.
reliability_note: Deploy is full-replace, not incremental. A slow link makes each publish expensive. Free tier has no stated SLA and no published bandwidth ceiling, so behaviour at 1 TiB/day is unproven.
